---
title: "Choose a palette"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

Use the palette name as shown, for example `carto_pal(5, "Burg")` for hex codes or `scale_fill_carto_c(palette = "Burg")` for a continuous **ggplot2** fill scale.

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
metadata = rcartocolor::metacartocolors

for (type in c("Quantitative", "Diverging", "Qualitative", "Aggregation")) {
  palettes = metadata[metadata$Type == tolower(type), ]
  cat("\n\n## ", type, "\n\n", sep = "")

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(palettes))) {
    colors = rcartocolor::carto_pal(palettes$Max_n[i], palettes$Name[i])
    tiles = sprintf(
      '<span title="%s" style="width:.75em;height:1em;background:%s"></span>',
      colors, colors
    )
    swatches = sprintf(
      '<span class="d-inline-flex" role="img" aria-label="Hex colors %s">%s</span>',
      paste(colors, collapse = ", "), paste(tiles, collapse = "")
    )
    cat(sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<p class="d-flex flex-wrap align-items-center gap-2 mb-2">',
        '<strong style="width:6rem">%s</strong> ',
        '<span style="width:10rem">%s–%s colors</span>%s</p>\n'
      ),
      palettes$Name[i], palettes$Min_n[i], palettes$Max_n[i], swatches
    ))
  }
}
```

## Preview palettes in R

Use `display_carto_all()` to see every palette or `display_carto_all(colorblind_friendly = TRUE)` to filter to palettes flagged as [colorblind-friendly](https://jakubnowosad.com/colorblindcheck/articles/check_rcartocolor.html).
